skills.title: Tirith Policies
skills.summary: Write, validate and run Tirith policy-as-code checks on Terraform and OpenTofu plans, and add them to a CI pipeline.
skills.description: Tirith checks the plan your pipeline already produces against JSON policies and exits non-zero when a change breaks one. This skill helps your agent write those policies, run them against a document that should fail, read Tirith's results and exit codes, and add the check to GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Bitbucket Pipelines, Jenkins, Azure DevOps or CircleCI.
examplePrompts: Write a Tirith policy that fails the plan if any S3 bucket is public.
Add a Tirith check to our GitHub Actions workflow before terraform apply.
Why did the Tirith step fail in CI?

skills.title: Terraform Plan Review
skills.summary: Review a Terraform or OpenTofu plan and flag replacements and deletes before apply.
skills.description: Your agent reads a Terraform or OpenTofu plan and explains it before anyone applies it. Bundled Tirith policies flag deletes, replacements and data-holding resources at risk, and the report lists replacements and deletes first, by resource address, with the attribute that forces each replacement. Sensitive values are named, never printed, and the skill never runs apply.
examplePrompts: Review my Terraform plan and flag anything destructive.
What will this plan delete or replace?

skills.title: Terraform Deploy
skills.summary: Plan and apply Terraform or OpenTofu from your coding agent, with a separate approval before applying the exact plan you reviewed.
skills.description: Your agent finds the root module, backend and workspace, confirms the target with you, and runs init and plan. It reviews the saved plan with the terraform-plan-review skill and applies only that plan file, after you approve it in a separate question. It never uses -auto-approve, destroy or state commands, and asks twice when the target looks like production.
examplePrompts: Deploy this Terraform to the dev workspace.
Plan and apply the changes in envs/staging, but let me review the plan first.
prerequisites: Credentials for the provider your configuration uses

skills.title: Create a StackGuardian Workflow
skills.summary: Create a StackGuardian workflow for Terraform, OpenTofu or a custom step pipeline, from your git repository or a library template.
skills.description: Your agent asks whether the code comes from your own git repository or a StackGuardian library template, then walks you through the workflow group, cloud connector, variables and template inputs. You see every input with the value that will be used before anything is created. Creating a workflow does not deploy anything; a deployment happens when a run starts.
examplePrompts: Create a workflow for the Terraform in github.com/acme/infra, folder envs/staging, branch main.
Create an OpenTofu workflow from our repo that needs approval before every apply.
Set up a workflow that runs our Ansible playbook as a custom step.

skills.title: Update a StackGuardian Workflow
skills.summary: Change an existing StackGuardian workflow's connector, variables, schedules, approvals, runner or sizing. Only what you change is touched.
skills.description: Your agent finds the workflow, confirms it is the one you mean, and changes only the settings you ask for. For settings saved as a whole list, such as tags or schedules, it reads the current list first so adding one entry keeps the others. You confirm a summary before anything changes.
examplePrompts: Add a nightly 2 AM schedule to prod-vpc.
Require approval from alice@example.com or bob@example.com before prod-vpc applies.
prod-vpc runs keep running out of memory. Give them 4 GB.

skills.title: Upgrade a StackGuardian Workflow
skills.summary: Move a StackGuardian workflow to another template revision, with a dry run that shows every change first.
skills.description: Your agent finds the workflow and the revision to move to, and asks whether to keep your settings or reset to the template. A dry run shows how many settings would be added, changed or removed before anything is applied. You review template inputs, environment variables, the cloud connector and custom step settings, then confirm.
examplePrompts: Upgrade prod-vpc to the latest revision of its template.
What would change if I moved prod-vpc to revision 5 of its template?
Roll prod-vpc back to the previous template revision.

skills.title: Create a StackGuardian Stack
skills.summary: Create several related StackGuardian workflows together from a stack template, reviewing each workflow's inputs.
skills.description: Your agent helps you pick a stack template, then walks through each workflow's inputs one workflow at a time. Inputs that come from another workflow's output are filled in for you, and the agent says where each one comes from. Creating a stack does not deploy anything until you start it.
examplePrompts: Find a stack template that sets up a VPC, a security group and an EC2 instance.
Create a stack from that template in the staging group with our AWS staging connector.

skills.title: Create a StackGuardian Policy
skills.summary: Add a StackGuardian guardrail that blocks, warns on or requires approval for infrastructure changes.
skills.description: Your agent offers a library policy template when one fits, a Tirith rule it writes and explains back to you, or your own git repository of Rego or Tirith policies. You choose what happens when a rule fails, where the policy applies and who can approve. An organization-wide policy is confirmed explicitly.
examplePrompts: Block any deployment in the prod group that makes an S3 bucket public.
Warn when the estimated monthly cost of an EC2 instance goes over $100.

skills.title: Manage StackGuardian Secrets
skills.summary: Store, rotate or delete StackGuardian vault secrets and use them in workflows.
skills.description: Your agent stores a token, password or key in the StackGuardian vault and shows you how workflows refer to it by name. Before deleting a secret, it lists the workflows that mention it and deletes only after you agree. A secret's value can't be read back, only replaced.
examplePrompts: Store a GitHub token as a secret called GITHUB_TOKEN.
Rotate the DB_PASSWORD secret.
Delete the OLD_API_KEY secret. Which workflows still use it?
